title: Fish Kaomoji ><(((º> Copy & Paste Fish Text Art
meta_description: Copy and paste fish kaomoji and fish text art: ><>, <><, ><(((º>, Japanese fish like >゜))))彡, fish bones, swimming scenes and hieroglyph fish 𓆝 𓆟 𓆞.
hero_tagline: Fish drawn in text, from the three-key ><> to Japanese fish with a splashing tail. Click any fish to copy it.
intro: A fish kaomoji draws the fish side-on, so the direction matters: ><> swims right and <>< swims left. The > is the tail fin, the brackets ((( are scales, and º or ゜ is the eye. Japanese fish add 彡, a character that reads as a splash of water behind the tail. Every fish here is plain text, so it pastes into a caption, bio, comment or chat, and the longer ones make a divider between paragraphs. For fish as pictures rather than text, the 🐟 🐠 🐡 emoji are on the animal emoji page linked below.

faq.q: What does ><> mean in a text?
faq.a: It is a fish swimming to the right: > is the tail, < is the head. Written the other way round as <><, it is also the plain-text version of the Christian fish symbol, which is why it shows up in bios.

faq.q: What is the 彡 at the end of some fish?
faq.a: 彡 is a Chinese character made of three slanted strokes. Japanese kaomoji use it for motion or splashing, so >゜))))彡 is a fish darting through water.

faq.q: Why do the hieroglyph fish show as boxes?
faq.a: The reader's device has no font for the Egyptian hieroglyph block. The text fish like ><(((º> use only basic punctuation, so any font can draw them.
